gauntlet_v2/docs/secure-boot/PAOS_ENROLL.excerpt:
**Before you start:** find your computer's one-time boot-menu key. The maker's logo shows it briefly when the
computer starts, for example "Press <F7> to Boot Menu". It's often F7, F8, F11 or F12, and F7 on AMI firmware.
Many computers ship with **Fast Boot** on. With Fast Boot on, a plain restart can skip the USB drive entirely and
start your usual system again, so use the boot-menu key.

## Steps

1. Plug in the PAOS-BOOT drive and restart. While the maker's logo shows, press the one-time boot-menu key it names (often F7, F8, F11 or F12; F7 on AMI firmware) and choose the USB / PAOS-BOOT entry. With Fast Boot on, a plain restart can skip the USB drive and start your usual system again: if that happens, restart and press the boot-menu key.

- **The fingerprint looks different.** First check the format: MokManager prints two lines of upper-case pairs, and the
  guide prints the same two lines. If the bytes differ, don't enroll: press Esc and choose "Continue boot".
- **The screen asks for a password.** You're on a different route: someone staged a request, for example with
  `mokutil --import`. This guide never asks for a password. Choose "Continue boot", and ask whoever prepared the
  computer.
- **You cancelled.** Nothing changed. Repeat from step 1 whenever you like.

Don't turn Secure Boot off, and don't enroll a key whose fingerprint is different.

**What you need:** the drive (volume) named **PAOS-BOOT**, with the file **PAOS_ENROLL_THIS_KEY.cer** at its top level,
and the `PAOS_ENROLL_GUIDE.txt` from that drive. That file shows this key's subject, its full SHA-256 fingerprint, and
the SHA-1 fingerprint that MokManager's "View key" screen displays. MokManager shows that SHA-1 under `[Fingerprint]`
as **two lines of upper-case byte pairs, 10 pairs per line** (for example `9D 71 33 19 9B 90 5F F9 17 9C` over
`F9 0B C7 2D FC 68 9F 83 11 6B`). The guide prints it the same way, as the two lines under its
`MokManager [Fingerprint]` heading. Compare the SHA-1; MokManager doesn't show the SHA-256.

4. The "Perform MOK management" menu opens. Choose "Enroll key from disk".
5. Choose the volume whose name starts with PAOS-BOOT. Ignore long technical lines such as PciRoot(0)/Pci(...)/HD(...): those are your computer's other disks.
6. Choose the file PAOS_ENROLL_THIS_KEY.cer. It is listed first; do not choose the guide or manifest files.
7. Choose "View key 0". Check that the subject contains "PaOS Forge" and that the two lines under [Fingerprint] match the two "MokManager [Fingerprint]" lines printed in this guide (upper case, 10 byte pairs per line). If they do not match, press Esc and choose "Continue boot" without enrolling.
8. Press Esc to leave the key view, choose "Continue", then "Yes" to "Enroll the key(s)?". No password is asked on this route.

7. Choose "View key 0". Check that the subject contains "PaOS Forge" and that the two lines under [Fingerprint] match the two "MokManager [Fingerprint]" lines printed in this guide (upper case, 10 byte pairs per line). If they do not match, press Esc and choose "Continue boot" without enrolling.

- **The fingerprint looks different.** First check the format: MokManager prints two lines of upper-case pairs, and the
  guide prints the same two lines. If the bytes differ, don't enroll: press Esc and choose "Continue boot".
- **The screen asks for a password.** You're on a different route: someone staged a request, for example with
  `mokutil --import`. This guide never asks for a password. Choose "Continue boot", and ask whoever prepared the
  computer.

;   Apply   the chosen zone takes effect through the check TZSET uses
;           (clock_zone_select: a seeded wall outside the pinned rule interval
;           refuses and nothing changes) and is saved the way TZSET saves it
;           (clock_prefs_persist: the MACed PaOSClockPrefs record, written only
;           when the zone changed, then read back). Fixed keeps the fixed offset
;           already in force.
;   Cancel  the list shows the zone in force again. Nothing is written.
;   Reset   the shipped default (fixed UTC-07:00) is applied and saved.
; The status line says what happened: Current / Saved / Unchanged <zone>, or
; that the zone applies until restart only (no store this boot), or that the
; save failed (the zone still applies), or the refusal.

jc   .repick
    call stp_sel                        ; Apply
    test eax, eax
    js   .choose
    cmp  eax, STP_ROW_FIXED
    je   .fixed
    lea  edi, [rax + 1]
    call clock_zone_select
    jc   .refused
    jmp  .applied
.fixed:
    mov  byte [rel clock_tz_zone], 0    ; the fixed offset in force stays
    jmp  .applied
.reset:
    mov  dword [rel clock_tz_min], STP_DEFAULT_MIN
    mov  byte [rel clock_tz_zone], 0
    xor  eax, eax                       ; L2: and the layout list to en-US
    call stp_kbd_mark
.applied:
    mov  word [rel clock_last_hhmm], 0xFFFF ; the next taskbar tick repaints, as after TZSET
    call clock_prefs_persist            ; EAX -1: the write or its readback failed
    push rax
    call stp_zone_row
    call stp_mark_row
    call stp_kbd_apply                  ; RCQ-38 L2: then the layout -> ECX its answer
    pop  rax
    lea  rsi, [rel stp_s_save_failed]
    test eax, eax
    jnz  stp_say
